title: ～てくれる — “someone does ～ for me”
summary: Shows that someone does something for you (or your family). Add くれる to the te-form; the person who does it is the subject.

patterns.gloss: Verb te-form + くれる (手伝ってくれる)

body.p: The giver is the subject and the receiver (me) is often left out: 兄が宿題を手伝ってくれた. It implies gratitude.
I do for others: ～てあげる. Others do for me: ～てくれる. I receive from others: ～てもらう. For a superior doing something for you, use ～てくださる.

examples.ja: 兄（あに）が宿題（しゅくだい）を手伝（てつだ）ってくれました。
examples.romaji: Ani ga shukudai o tetsudatte kuremashita.
examples.tr: My older brother helped me with my homework.

examples.ja: 友達（ともだち）が重（おも）い荷物（にもつ）を持（も）ってくれました。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi ga omoi nimotsu o motte kuremashita.
examples.tr: My friend carried the heavy luggage for me.

examples.ja: 店員（てんいん）が親切（しんせつ）に道（みち）を教（おし）えてくれた。
examples.romaji: Ten'in ga shinsetsu ni michi o oshiete kureta.
examples.tr: The shop clerk kindly told me the way.

pitfalls: The helper is the subject, not me.
For superiors use くださる rather than くれる.
